gates.detail: Example sentence capitals/punctuation and contains the word.

issues: Illustration brief says a butterfly comes out of a 'cocoon'; butterflies emerge from a chrysalis (moths make cocoons). This contradicts the science-themed example.
'recording' is not a true synonym. It can also mean an audio-only recording, which may confuse young learners.
'videotape' is an outdated word that children aged 6-8 are unlikely to know, so it adds little value to the word family.
Spelling guidance is unclear. 'Two vowel sounds at the end' does not match the letter breakdown, and it never mentions that the word has three vowels (i, e, o).
The category 'Arts and Culture' fits poorly; videos are more about media and technology.
suggested_fixes: Change 'cocoon' to 'chrysalis', or simply say 'coming out and spreading its wings'.
Replace 'recording' with a closer synonym, or remove it and keep 'film' and 'clip'.
Replace 'videotape' with 'videos' only, or add 'video call' as the child-relevant form.
Rewrite the spelling guidance as: 'Say it in parts: vid-ee-oh. Spell it v-i-d-e-o. It ends with the letters e and o.'
Change the category to 'Technology and Media'.
